tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrap correctly scaffolded WinUI 3 project, copied 121 files, injected TODO markers, and generated MIGRATION-MAPPING.md. Agent completed migration successfully on first attempt.
Caught two issues the agent missed: residue UWP comment in Styles.xaml (L313) and all 121 MIGRATION-MAPPING.md rows stuck at Status=copied. Agent fixed both and re-ran to PASS.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP AdaptiveStreaming sample uses Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient for IHttpFilter-based request modification. The migrated code retains Windows.Web.Http usings, but .NET SDK ImplicitUsings injects System.Net.Http into scope.
failed_apis.root_cause: CS0104 ambiguous reference. .NET SDK projects with <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> auto-import System.Net.Http, which conflicts with Windows.Web.Http types (HttpClient, HttpRequestMessage, HttpResponseMessage) used by the UWP sample.
failed_apis.fix: Agent added <Using Remove="System.Net.Http" /> to the .csproj ItemGroup, which resolved all 14+ CS0104 errors in one shot.

special_apis.special_handling: IHttpFilter implementations (e.g. AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger, AddAuthorizationHeaderFilter) use Windows.Web.Http types that conflict with System.Net.Http under ImplicitUsings. Must remove the System.Net.Http implicit using or fully qualify all Windows.Web.Http types.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'HttpClient' is an ambiguous reference between 'System.Net.Http.HttpClient' and 'Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient' (14+ occurrences across 6 files)
errors_encountered.root_cause: .NET SDK ImplicitUsings auto-imports System.Net.Http, conflicting with Windows.Web.Http types used by the UWP sample's IHttpFilter-based network stack.

errors_encountered.error: CS0535: 'AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger' does not implement interface member 'IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync(HttpRequestMessage)'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Caused by the same HttpClient ambiguity — the compiler couldn't resolve HttpRequestMessage to the correct Windows.Web.Http type.
errors_encountered.fix: Resolved automatically when the System.Net.Http implicit using was removed.

dev_agent_struggles.where: Final build verification (outer agent, post-validator PASS)
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent ran 'winapp build 2>&1 | Select-String -Pattern error|warning...' which returned BUILD_EXIT=1 but no error details (Select-String swallowed all output). Then ran 'dotnet build' piped through Select-String, which hung for 4+ read_powershell retries (120s, 60s, 60s, 90s, 120s) before agent killed the shell.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 5 retries over ~7 minutes of wall time
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Select-String filter swallowed build output the same way Where-Object does. The skill warns about Where-Object but not Select-String.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent stopped the shell and re-ran with 'dotnet build --no-incremental 2>&1 | Where-Object { $_ -match "error CS|Build (succeeded|failed)" }' which worked because there were matching lines.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Skill should warn about ALL output-filtering cmdlets (Select-String, Where-Object, etc.) or recommend 'winapp build' exclusively.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Build failed with 17 errors (14 CS0104, 2 CS0535, 1 WMC9999) all stemming from System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http conflict.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 1 turn — agent diagnosed and fixed immediately
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: ImplicitUsings adds System.Net.Http which conflicts with Windows.Web.Http. Skill only covers CS0104 for Windows.UI.Xaml vs Microsoft.UI.Xaml types (LaunchActivatedEventArgs).
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Add a dedicated CS0104 subsection for System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http conflict in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, specifically mentioning the ImplicitUsings mechanism.

env_issues.issue: Smoke launch in validator reported WARN: 'winapp run did not register the app (no AUMID, no PID) - Failed to register package... error 0x80070003'
env_issues.workaround: Validator correctly treated this as a non-fatal WARN (environment/deploy issue, not a migration defect). App was launched successfully by the parity checker separately.
